A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pFedMMA study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Moved and renumbered material can be matched, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification experiments across eleven datasets, together with ablations, learning curves, and measured computational costs in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated PEFT baselines, modality-aggregation ablations, and AdamW results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1 replace v2's uniform server averaging with weights proportional to client dataset size. This revises one algorithmic step; the adapter architecture, local loss, and personalized/shared parameter split remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eleven datasets and base-to-novel, personalization, and label/domain-shift scenarios. The new optimizer and modality controls reuse existing coverage. Appendix B.4's discussion of unseen-domain generalization does not introduce an evaluation.

E2.justification: V3 adds FedCLIP-Adapter (Gao et al., 2024) and FedCLIP-LoRA (Zanella and Ben Ayed, 2024) to Table 1's seven-dataset, 16-shot comparison. This substantially broadens the prompt-focused comparison to two PEFT families directly relevant to the proposed adapter method. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V3 adds an AdamW evaluation at 16 shots across seven datasets (Table 19) and modality-aggregation controls at 16 shots across four datasets (Table 18). Existing partitions, client participation, training budgets, backbones, and default SGD settings are retained.

E4.justification: Tables 6 and 18 newly test vision-only, text-only, and separate vision/text aggregation against unified multimodal sharing. Table 19 adds optimizer sensitivity evidence. Earlier dimension, scaling, insertion-layer, personalization-sharing, and local-only ablations remain.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 in both versions reports three runs with different random seeds and averages across clients. V3 introduces no changed run counts, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the existing figures are retained.

E6.justification: Earlier score entries are retained, but substantial comparator and supplementary result sets are added. Table 1 reports average HM values of 80.04 for FedCLIP-Adapter and 83.35 for FedCLIP-LoRA alongside pFedMMA's retained 84.15. The four-dataset aggregation study reports 79.70 versus 79.31–79.39 for variants. Table 19 newly reports pFedMMA's 84.58 under AdamW, a different optimizer setting.

T1.justification: The formal aggregation definition changes from a uniform mean to a dataset-size-weighted mean in Section 3.2 and Algorithm 1; these differ when client dataset sizes differ. No new theorem, assumption, proof, or cost derivation is introduced. The added harmonic-mean formula merely explains the existing metric.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement withdraw the claim that pFedMMA is the first personalized multimodal-adapter or adapter-based VLM framework. The principal claims about personalization–generalization balance, communication efficiency, and performance against federated prompt methods remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets the modality-ablation averages as evidence for a slightly stronger, more stable information-sharing mechanism through a unified projection. Appendix B.4 clarifies the personalized-model setting and distinguishes it from learning one global model for unseen domains.

D1.justification: V3 adds a reported code-access link in the abstract and specifies that the new federated PEFT baselines update and aggregate only adapter or low-rank layers. Hardware, software, and computational-cost information were already documented in v2.

R1.justification: New Appendix B.4 discusses federated out-of-distribution and domain generalization, including FedDAT and PLAN, and explains their treatment as complementary work rather than direct baselines. Additional citations support this positioning and the harmonic-mean rationale; most earlier related-work discussion remains.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. V3 adds focused explanations, acknowledgments, Appendix B.4, and a main-text cost subsection reusing Appendix E material. Headings and citations receive limited edits, although the FedPGP citation in Appendix B.2 becomes an unresolved question mark.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains baseline rows; v3 adds Tables 6/18 for aggregation variants and Table 19 for AdamW. V2's appendix cost table is also displayed as main-text Table 7. Conference headers, typography, and float placement change, while all five figures and most table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's prompt-focused evaluation, v3 adds relevant adapter/LoRA comparisons and focused checks of modality sharing and optimizer dependence. Withdrawing the 'first' claim and clarifying the PFL/FedDG distinction improve precision. These are bounded gains: the added PEFT comparisons cover only 16 shots, and the small modality-ablation differences lack dispersion estimates, limiting the stronger stability interpretation.
